A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATLAS study. All 29 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual training experiments, scaling-law evaluations in Table 1, language-transfer measurements and pretraining-versus-finetuning results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the experiment inventory in Table B.1 and extended results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Equation (2) replaces the common saturation parameter lambda with lambda_t, lambda_i and lambda_other. However, the accompanying prose still explicitly says the parameter is shared across data sources. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether independently fitted parameters were introduced or only the notation changed.

E1.justification: The MADLAD-400 and Flores evaluation coverage, language sets, and monolingual, bilingual, multilingual and finetuning tasks are unchanged. Appendices B and C introduce no additional coverage in v2.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Chinchilla, Data-Constrained and Multilingual Scaling Law comparators in their respective comparisons. The ATLAS variants and pretraining-versus-finetuning comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The held-out evaluation dimensions, data splits, model sizes, training budgets and sampling procedures remain unchanged. Section 2 newly mentions varying compute C, but this was already part of v1's documented experiments.

E4.justification: The data-term ablations in Table 1, transfer-symmetry and linguistic-similarity analyses, and transfer-versus-scale analyses in Figure C.1 are retained without additions or substantive revisions.

E5.justification: The significance reporting in Figure 3, seed-stability discussion in Appendix B.2 and cross-validation reporting in Appendix B.6 are unchanged. No repeated-run counts or uncertainty-reporting procedures are added.

E6.justification: Figure 7's caption changes the reported crossover relationship from log(C) = 10283128 × N^1.65 to C = 10283128 × N^1.65, with corresponding plot-label corrections. Tabulated scores and empirical curves remain unchanged. The plot still uses exponent 1.54, and Section 6 retains a different formula, so the reporting correction is incomplete.

T1.justification: Equation (2)'s source-indexed saturation parameters could revise the mathematical parameter-sharing assumption, but the unchanged shared-parameter statement prevents distinguishing a substantive revision from a notation inconsistency. The capacity-scaling and iso-loss derivations in Appendix B.7 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contribution claims about ATLAS, language transfer, multilingual capacity and pretraining-versus-finetuning crossover points. The added conclusion summarizes claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning script similarity, asymmetric transfer and model capacity remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same qualifications about checkpoint mixtures, training duration and omitted data repetition; the conclusion adds no substantive limitation or mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same hyperparameters, model dimensions, language-sampling rates and experimental instructions. The new reference to Appendix B.3 improves navigation without disclosing additional technical settings or resources.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to earlier scaling-law research are unchanged. Section 2 adds attribution for R-squared evaluation to already-cited works without changing the research comparison.

P1.justification: v2 adds a conclusion, explains the scaling-law coefficients in Section 3, adds an appendix cross-reference and makes small wording corrections. Most prose and the existing narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds conference headers, groups Equations (1)–(3) on page 4, and moves Figure 7 from page 9 to page 10 while correcting its axis, inset and caption labels from log(C) to C. Other figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The conclusion, coefficient explanations and Figure 7 label corrections improve exposition. However, Equation (2) introduces ambiguity about a central method parameter by conflicting with the retained shared-lambda prose, and the crossover formulas remain inconsistent. With unchanged empirical evidence, these limited benefits and methodological ambiguity do not establish a reliable net improvement.
